tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H36): GEMM1 epilogue on all warps (4 per TMEM quadrant, A&S erfc GELU) in tc_kernel and sc_kernel; 4,96 added to the sc table; GEMM2 cta_group::2 as the stretch. Target rows: 16,384 / 8,384 / 32,768 / 16,768 / 8,768 / 2,768 (tc_kernel) and 4,192 / 8,192 / 4,96 (sc_kernel). get_kernel on either parent exceeds the tool limit: request the card and the sources in parts. STEP 0 (<= 8 B200 min): add 4,96,56,56 to sc_kernel's dispatch table (the C=96 56x56 instantiation exists; B=4 only changes the tile table) and, if the C=320 32x32 instantiation compiles without new code paths (4096-B planes, 4C = 1280 = 20 N-chunks of 64, 5 K-blocks), 8,320 too; run_tests with r7-merge as the same-container control; keep each row only if it beats the merge path by >= 2 us rented. STEP 1 (stamps): TC_STAMPS on tc_kernel at 16,384 and 8,384 from the epilogue warps (per-tile post-accumulator time, expected 11.7 / 10.9 us) and on sc_kernel at 8,192 (3 x 3.9 us); record them as the baseline. STEP 2 (the experiment): after the accumulator-full barrier of each GEMM1 tile, run the epilogue on every warp of the CTA (12 now; go to 16 warps / 512 threads if registers stay <= 128 with STACK 0): warp w serves TMEM lanes 32*(w%4)..+31 and the column slice (w/4) of the tile, each thread keeps two tcgen05.ld of 16-32 columns in flight, applies the LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + v, the A&S erfc GELU (the form used by G r7 and A r5, |err| <= 1.2e-6 in h), accumulates its per-(image,k) sumsq partial in registers and combines partials across the column-slice warps through smem (one value per lane per quadrant) before the existing red.add / store; keep the staged coalesced h stores. Check cuobjdump: STACK 0, no LDL/STL, registers; stamp again at the same rows. STEP 3: interleaved x3 vs the parent in one container (harness_time) at 16,384 / 8,384 / 32,768 / 8,768 / 4,192 / 8,192. STEP 4 (stretch, only if >= 15 B200 min remain): port the r6 cta_group::2 recipe to GEMM2 (cluster 2x1, each CTA loads half of the B token tile, leader-only MMA, multicast commit) and measure the GEMM2 wait / B-tile scale term at 8,192 and 8,768. STEP 5: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, and the PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, torch.manual_seed(200), 10 rounds, max |err| and beyond-own-atol count) for every changed path (all 12 rows). Report per-row rented times vs the parent, the per-tile epilogue before/after, registers, and which rows the merge should take. Success: In one container vs the parent: per-tile post-accumulator epilogue down >= 40 % at 16,384 and 8,384; rows 16,384 <= 48, 8,384 <= 32, 32,768 <= 58 us rented (D takes 32,768 from A), no row slower than the parent by > 1 us; 16/16 pass; 0 beyond-own-atol on every changed path. Refuted if: Doubling the epilogue warps cuts the per-tile post-accumulator time by < 25 % with STACK 0 and no spills: then the epilogue is bound by TMEM-load or store latency per warp, not by warp count, and the next lever is restructuring the loads (report the stamps and the SASS mix). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) every red.add / atomic target, old or new (gsq per (image,k), split-K output), must be zeroed or prefilled inside the launch before the grid sync that precedes its first use, as r6/r7 do; the workspace is torch.empty (uninitialised). (b) TMA descriptors encoded on every call, as now. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.

Experiment E2 (tests H37): Fused pass-1 pipeline instantiated for 8,320 (streamed W1', 64-token tiles) and 4,96 (112-token tiles with a masked warp tile). Rows 8,320,32,32 and 4,96,56,56 only; the 64,96 / 32,128 paths stay as shipped and must time within noise of the parent. STEP 1, 4,96: tiles of R=2 image rows = 112 tokens padded to 128 (four 32-token warp tiles, the fourth half-masked: zero the padded d columns and skip their stores and sumsq), 112 CTAs; W1' (74 KB) resident as at 64,96; reuse the 56x56 TMA halo staging. Time pass 1, K3 and the batched swap-AB cuBLASLt GEMM2 (7.3 us measured at 4 batches); compare with the merge path (A, 46.8 rented in r7's container) interleaved x3. STEP 2, 8,320: C=320 makes W1' 819 KB, so stream it per 128-hidden-row block (80 KB fp16 per block, 10 blocks) through a double-buffered cp.async.bulk ring from the fp16 W1' scratch written by K0, double-buffered against the mma loop; d tile 64 tokens x 320 channels fp16 (40 KB); try R=2 (64-token tiles, 128 CTAs) first and R=1 (32-token tiles, 256 items, 2 per CTA) if the per-tile chain is latency-bound; GEMM2 batched swap-AB at HW=1024 with 8 batches (check the heuristic kernel and time it cold). Stamp pass 1 per tile (ingest wait, mma, GELU, stores) from the working warps. STEP 3: run_tests 16/16 (portal-order check) with r7-merge as the same-container control; PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for both new rows. STEP 4 (stretch, only if >= 12 B200 min remain): the balanced erf (I30): route one third of the elements through an FMA-only minimax erf polynomial (|err| <= 5e-7, clamped) and measure the GEMM side alone at 64,96 and 32,128. Report per-row rented times, the per-tile stamps, registers/smem per instantiation, and which rows the merge should take. Success: In one container vs r7-merge: 4,96 <= 36 us rented (merge path 46.8) and 8,320 <= 55 us (78.6), 16/16 pass, 0 beyond-own-atol on both rows, the two large rows unchanged within 2 %. Refuted if: 4,96 with 112 tiles is not faster than the merge path, or 8,320 pass 1 exceeds 45 us with the W1' ring stamped as overlapped (then the serial per-tile chain, not SM count, binds and the fused structure does not transfer to C >= 320). You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): (a) the GRN sums and any new red.add target must be zeroed by K0 in the same call (as r7 does); the fp16 W1' scratch for the 8,320 ring is written by K0 in the same call, never kept from an earlier call. (b) cuBLASLt: only the heuristic result may be cached per shape; descriptors, batch strides and pointers set on every call, as r7 does. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.

Experiment E3 (tests H38): New design: image-counter dataflow persistent tcgen05 kernel (work queue, no grid barrier) for the B >= 8 wide-C rows. Rows 8,768 / 16,768 / 32,768 (7x7, C=768) and 8,384 / 16,384 (14x14, C=384); other rows run the r0 anchor fallback (merge-only candidate). Read the notebook and the lineage conclusions (D, B, F, C) first: the engine and the counter protocol are both documented there. STEP 0 (<= 5 min): queue/counter microbench, 148 cooperative CTAs with stub items (32 KB bulk copy each) in the proposed order and per-image gating, at B = 8 and 32, vs two flat-counter barriers; record the span and the median claim-to-start latency (expect <= 1 us). STEP 1 (engine, <= 15 min): a self-contained tcgen05 kind::f16 swap-AB tile (A = 128 weight rows K-major via a 128B-swizzled TMA box, B = activations [channel][token] MN-major with the validated descriptor: LBO 8192, SBO 1024, +2048 per k16; 4-stage ring; whole-warp TMA and MMA roles with elect.sync; accumulator in TMEM; tcgen05.ld with two loads in flight per thread), validated bit-close against torch (fp32 matmul of the fp16 operands, max err <= 2e-5) at 768x196x384 and 384x196x1536, warm L2, before any fusion. STEP 2 (kernel): one cooperative launch, 148 CTAs x 384-512 threads, 1 CTA/SM, dynamic smem set to the maximum over all shapes at module load. Workspace from torch.empty: queue head, w_done, conv_done[B], g1_done[B], departure counter, plus the fp16 W1'/W2 scratch, d16 and LN partials, hidden [k][token] fp16, gsq[B][4C]. Items in the static queue, claimed by atomicAdd on the head: (i) weight units: W1' = fp16(lnw-folded W1) with u = W1.lnw and c1 = W1.lnb + b1, W2 fp16, b2' = W2.gb + b2 and the out = x + b2' prefill (16-B loads/stores, spread over all CTAs); (ii) conv units: bulk-plane 7x7 / 14x14 depthwise conv of one plane group of ONE image plus per-token LN partials, so conv_done[b] counts units of image b; (iii) GEMM1 tiles (128 hidden rows x the tokens of one image, image-major): wait w_done == W units and conv_done[b] == units(b) with an ld.acquire poll, run the tile, epilogue = LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + c1, exact erf GELU (A&S erfc form accepted), per-(image,k) sumsq thread-local (lane = k) red.add into gsq[b][k], fp16 h stores coalesced through smem, then red.release.gpu on g1_done[b]; (iv) GEMM2 tiles (128 output channels x image tokens x split-K slice, image-major): wait g1_done[b] == tiles1(b), compute s_b = 1 + gw*gf/(mean gf + eps) from gsq[b] (one round, all loads issued first), scale the fp16 B stage in smem after it lands (fence.proxy.async before the MMA) or use D's two-accumulator form, red.global.add.v4 into out. The last departing CTA zeroes every counter so the workspace is correct for the next call. Keep every role warp-uniform; stamp phases from the working warps; check cuobjdump STACK 0. Compile with target_hardware [B200] only. STEP 3: stamps at 16,384 and 32,768 showing GEMM2 items of early images starting before the last GEMM1 items, and the per-CTA idle (spin) time. STEP 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check, r7-merge as the same-container control, PRECISION LOG (fp64 reference, harness generators, seed 200, 10 rounds) for the five rows. Report per-row rented times vs the merge, the stamps, the microbench, registers/smem, and which rows (if any) the merge should take; negative results in full. Success: First build correct on all five rows and, in one container vs r7-merge, >= 5 us faster on at least one of 16,384 / 32,768 / 8,384 with stamps showing GEMM2 items running before the last GEMM1 items; 0 beyond-own-atol. Incubation line: within 15 % of the merge on 16,384 and 8,384 with the overlap visible in the stamps keeps the lineage alive for r9. Refuted if: With a validated engine, the packed kernel is slower than the merge by > 10 % on every B >= 8 wide-C row AND the stamps show the GEMM1 tails are not filled by GEMM2 or conv items (then the dataflow family is closed for the wide-C rows, and the remaining value is in the engine terms D already owns). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules, overrides the counter placement above): (a) torch.empty memory is uninitialised and is not guaranteed to be the same memory or unchanged between calls, so the queue head, w_done, conv_done[B], g1_done[B] and the departure counter must NOT live in the torch.empty workspace relying on the previous call's reset. Put them in a module-level __device__ buffer (zero-initialised at module load, sized for the largest B), reset by the last departing CTA after every other CTA has departed; or zero them with cudaMemsetAsync on the current stream immediately before the launch. (b) gsq[b][4C] and every other red.add target must be zeroed inside this call before its first add, ordered by a counter the adding items already wait on (e.g. zeroed in the weight units and covered by w_done). (c) W1'/W2/b2' scratch is rebuilt every call by the weight units (no converted weights kept across calls); TMA descriptors encoded every call. (d) Spin-waits rely on all CTAs being co-resident: cooperative launch with grid <= SM count, and every queue item may only wait on items with lower queue indices. (c) No PDL; launch_with_pdl stays false. Stamps compiled out of the shipped build (the timed path writes no stamp buffer). target_hardware [B200] only. No state carried between calls except shape-keyed attributes/plans.
